lyrics:
[Intro: a cappella four-part harmony, no instruments]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard

[Verse 1: warm male voice, acoustic guitar]
I've had the kind of money where you don't check the price
Had the kind of trouble where you don't sleep nights
Neither one of them taught me a thing
Like a Saturday with nothing to bring but

[Chorus: full band, fiddle, group singalong]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard
Radio on the windowsill, a ballgame from afar
Sun going down like it's got no place to be
A paid-off truck, a porch, and my people around me
It ain't much, and it's all I need

[Verse 2: voice and band, relaxed]
Granddad's skillet, black as a crow
Fed four generations, never touched soap
He'd say, "Rich is a table where nobody's missing"
I didn't get it then. Granddad, I'm listening.

[Chorus: full band, fiddle, group singalong]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard
Radio on the windowsill, a ballgame from afar
Sun going down like it's got no place to be
A paid-off truck, a porch, and my people around me
It ain't much, and it's all I need

[Bridge: band drops, fiddle and voice, slower]
Here's to the nurse on the night shift, the lineman in the storm
The teacher buying pencils, keeping thirty kids warm
The ones who keep it running so the rest of us can sit
We'll save you a plate. You've earned it.

[Final Chorus: a cappella first line, then full band]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard
Radio on the windowsill, a ballgame from afar
Sun going down like it's got no place to be
A paid-off truck, a porch, and my people around me
It ain't much, and it's all I need

[Outro: fiddle tune, a screen door, children laughing]
